texts.orig: 1. Open PM and engineering roles are trending up
texts.text: 1. Open PM and engineering roles are trending up

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In spite of what you’re hearing about recessions and AI taking jobs, open roles for product managers and engineers at tech companies are
texts.text: In spite of what you’re hearing about recessions and AI taking jobs, open roles for product managers and engineers at tech companies are

texts.label: text
texts.orig: increasing
texts.text: increasing

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There are over 6,000 open PM roles globally right now—53.6% above the bottom we saw in 2023, and already up 11% since the start of the year. This is the most open PM roles we’ve seen in over two years.
texts.text: There are over 6,000 open PM roles globally right now—53.6% above the bottom we saw in 2023, and already up 11% since the start of the year. This is the most open PM roles we’ve seen in over two years.

texts.orig: 2. AI roles are exploding
texts.text: 2. AI roles are exploding

texts.label: text

texts.orig: 3. Layoffs are slowing
texts.text: 3. Layoffs are slowing

texts.label: text
texts.orig: More good news: We’re on track to see fewer layoffs this year than in the past four years. However, the possibility of future cuts is ever-present, even at the most respected companies.
texts.text: More good news: We’re on track to see fewer layoffs this year than in the past four years. However, the possibility of future cuts is ever-present, even at the most respected companies.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 4. Capital investment is increasing
texts.text: 4. Capital investment is increasing

texts.label: text
texts.orig: We’re seeing more capital investment (e.g. GPUs, data centers, etc.) this year than ever (+29% from last year, +227% from five years ago). It’s still unclear if this only means more hardware or whether it will also lead to more jobs, but I’d rather see this than have it going in the other direction.
texts.text: We’re seeing more capital investment (e.g. GPUs, data centers, etc.) this year than ever (+29% from last year, +227% from five years ago). It’s still unclear if this only means more hardware or whether it will also lead to more jobs, but I’d rather see this than have it going in the other direction.

texts.orig: 6. Remote work opportunities are declining
texts.text: 6. Remote work opportunities are declining

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The number of roles that allow you to work remotely continues to decline. At remote work’s peak in late 2022, we saw about 35% listed open PM roles as remote-friendly. Today, only 23% have a remote option.
texts.text: The number of roles that allow you to work remotely continues to decline. At remote work’s peak in late 2022, we saw about 35% listed open PM roles as remote-friendly. Today, only 23% have a remote option.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The trend is clear, and we’re probably near the new baseline of around 20% of roles being remote-friendly.
